paragraphs: R. Chinena bar Idi: Taanit 7a. Moed Katan 5a has Rav Chinena—son of Rav Idi, as in Ein Yaakov—and Rav Yehoshua son of Rav Idi; perhaps his brother. Rav Chinena bar Idi asked Rav Adda bar Ahavah, who answered, etc. He said, “But Rav Chinena the Elder said: R. Assi said, etc.”: Pesachim 75a. He sat before Rav Adda bar Ahavah and said: a gentile who brought a trough full [of jars], with one kilbit [fish] in one of them, etc. He asked, “Whence do you have this?” He answered, “I heard this matter from three ‘Scriptures’: Rav, Shmuel, and R. Yochanan.” Rashi explains: three great sages worthy of reliance like Scripture; see there. Yuchasin also listed R. Chanina bar Idi; they are all one. “Shmuel's student”—I do not know the basis. If it is because he said, “I heard from three Scriptures, Rav, Shmuel, and R. Yochanan,” then Rav and R. Yochanan should also be his teachers. Mekhilta, Beshalach, VaYavo Amalek, section 2, has Chananyah ben Idi. Mishpatim, chapter 5: R. Acha says, etc.; R. Chanina ben Idi says. I am uncertain whether this is the same man, since R. Yishmael, who arranged the Mekhilta, long preceded Rav Adda bar Ahavah.
